title: Cocartesian recognition from represented mixed mapping spaces
statement:
Use quasicategories, coherent functors, standard simplices, mapping spaces and equivalences of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], inner fibrations, fibres and cocartesian edges of [def-coef-infinity-fibrations], and mapping-space composition of [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. Let $p:E\to\Delta^1$ be an inner fibration of small quasicategories and put $C=E\times_{\Delta^1}\{0\}$ and $D=E\times_{\Delta^1}\{1\}$. For $x\in C$ and $y\in D$, write $\operatorname{Map}^{01}_E(x,y)$ for the homotopy fibre over the unique edge $0\to1$ of the induced map on mapping spaces.

Suppose that for every $x\in C$ a vertex $T_x\in D$ and equivalences of spaces
$$\epsilon_{x,y}:\operatorname{Map}^{01}_E(x,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_D(T_x,y)$$
are given, coherently natural in $y\in D$. Naturality includes compatibility with postcomposition by all arrows of $D$ and its higher simplices; no functor $C\to D$ is assumed in this hypothesis.

Then $p$ is a cocartesian fibration. For every edge $e:x\to y$ over $0\to1$, the edge $e$ is $p$-cocartesian if and only if the component represented by $\epsilon_{x,y}(e)$ is an equivalence in $D$. In particular, an edge corresponding to the identity of $T_x$ is a cocartesian lift of $0\to1$ with target $T_x$, up to the specified mapping-space identification. No nonemptiness or limit or colimit hypothesis on either fibre is imposed.

source.place: Higher Topos Theory, Proposition 2.4.4.3 (opposite-category dual), printed p. 131 in the cited edition: homotopy-pullback mapping criterion. The represented mixed-mapping specialization and inverse test are expanded by the agent; they isolate the recognition argument in former step 4 of the item, following Higher Algebra Lemma 4.2.2.20 and Remark 4.2.2.21. Read online; WANTED: archived HTT in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical criterion.
